title: Rafael and the Bell
premise: Folklorist Lior Vane returns to the fog-bound village of Rafael's Hollow to record its songs, only to find the villagers refuse to sing any verse twice—and to find Rafael, the imaginary friend she invented at age seven, waiting on her porch exactly as she left him, thirty years unchanged. As she digs into the founders' papers, she learns the village was built on a bargain: a child must be given to the bell in the chapel tower every generation, and her childhood self was chosen—Rafael was not imaginary, but a memory-keeper sent to make her forget. The ritual the founders started was never finished; it requires someone who remembers both lives, and time is running out as the villagers' faces begin to blur and the bell begins to ring on its own. In the climax, Lior enters the tower, sings the forbidden song twice, and offers herself—but instead binds Rafael into the bell in her place, freeing the village and erasing him from everyone's memory but hers. She leaves with her recordings intact and one song no one else will ever remember hearing.
about_author: Marguerite Blackwood is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories in coastal villages before turning to fiction. Her work blends folk horror with quiet domestic dread, exploring how communities survive by choosing what to forget.

chapters.title: The Song They Won't Sing Twice
chapters.summary: Lior Vane arrives in Rafael's Hollow with recording equipment and a list of songs collected from a defunct parish archive. Villagers are warm but evasive; when old Marta sings a harvest verse for her, she stops mid-line, pale, refusing to repeat it. That night Lior finds Rafael on her porch—unchanged since she was seven. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: uncanny homecoming, the comfort of recognition curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What the Founders Buried
chapters.summary: Lior searches the chapel records and finds the founders' ledger: a covenant binding the village to 'the Bell that remembers,' renewed each generation by giving it a child's name. Her own name appears, dated the year she left. Rafael appears inside locked rooms, insisting he kept her safe by making her forget. POV: Lior, with interpolated ledger entries. Emotional beat: investigation deepens into personal betrayal—the past she mourned was stolen from her.

chapters.title: Faces Going Soft
chapters.summary: The forgetting spreads: villagers call each other by wrong names, photographs blur, and the bell rings unstruck at dusk. Marta, half-dissolved, begs Lior to finish what the founders started before the Hollow forgets itself entirely. Rafael confesses he was made of her memories, sent back because the ritual is incomplete without someone who remembers both sides. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: rising panic and grief as identity itself becomes the stakes.

chapters.title: Twice-Sung
chapters.summary: Lior climbs the bell tower at midnight with Marta's completed verse and Rafael beside her. She sings the forbidden song twice, opening the covenant, and when the Bell demands its due she names Rafael instead of herself—giving the memory-keeper back his own existence. The tolling stops; the village wakes whole, remembering everything except him. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: sacrificial climax resolving into bittersweet release—she keeps one song, and one friend, that no one else can recall.
